s: A media company renders animation frames in a nightly batch that needs up to 4,000 vCPUs. Each frame takes 3-8 minutes to render and can be retried safely, and the batch must finish within 6 hours. The renderer runs on any current-generation x86 instance that has at least 8 vCPUs and 32 GiB of memory. The company currently uses On-Demand C5 instances in a single Availability Zone. Which solution will be MOST cost-effective while meeting the deadline?
o: Use an EC2 Auto Scaling group with a mixed instances policy that uses attribute-based instance type selection (at least 8 vCPUs and 32 GiB of memory). Launch Spot Instances across all Availability Zones with the price-capacity-optimized allocation strategy, and requeue frames from interrupted instances.
Launch Spot Instances of a single instance type in one Availability Zone with the lowest-price allocation strategy, and requeue frames from interrupted instances.
Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan that covers 4,000 vCPUs of C5 capacity, and keep running On-Demand Instances.
Request Spot Instances with a defined duration of 6 hours so that the instances are not interrupted during the batch.

w.y: Short, retryable frames are ideal for Spot Instances. Diversifying across many instance types through attribute-based selection and across all Availability Zones, with the price-capacity-optimized strategy, gives low prices with low interruption risk, so the batch stays within the deadline at the MOST cost-effective price.

o.A: Correct: diversified Spot with price-capacity-optimized balances cost and interruption risk.
o.B: A single pool maximizes interruption and capacity risk, endangering the 6-hour deadline.
o.C: The commitment is paid for 24 hours a day, but the workload runs only about 6 hours nightly, so most of it is wasted.
o.D: Spot Instances with a defined duration (Spot blocks) are no longer available.

d: MOST cost-effective while meeting the deadline
